claim: Nucleosomes comprise approximately 147 bp of DNA and a histone octamer formed by two copies of histone H2A-H2B and H3-H4 heterodimers.
source: The basic unit of chromatin is the nucleosome, which comprises ~147 bp of DNA and a histone octamer formed by two copies of histone H2A-H2B and H3-H4 heterodimers (Bentley et al., 1984; Kornberg and Thomas, 1974; Luger et al., 1997; Oudet et al., 1975).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior structural studies of nucleosomes.

claim: H3K4 di- and tri-methylation is catalyzed by the Set1 complex (also called the COMPASS complex).
source: H3K4 di- and tri-methylation (H3K4me2/3) is catalyzed by the Set1 complex (also called the COMPASS complex) and is associated with steady-state gene transcription; thus, H3K4me2/3 is considered to be an 'activating' mark in mammals.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and represents established knowledge about histone methylation.

claim: In budding yeast, most evidence indicates that H3K4 methylation is a repressive mark.
source: Conversely, in budding yeast, most of the evidence indicates that H3K4 methylation is a repressive mark (Shilatifard, 2006; Weiner et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: H3K36 tri-methylation by Set2 directs the deacetylation of histones, predominantly at the 3' portion of gene open reading frames, to suppress spurious intragenic transcription initiation.
source: H3K36 tri-methylation (H3K36me3) by Set2 directs the deacetylation of histones, predominantly at the 3' portion of gene open reading frames (ORFs), to suppress spurious intragenic transcription initiation (Carrozza et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Mutations at H3K79 as well as inactivation of its methyltransferase, Dot1, lead to loss of telomere silencing.
source: Methylation of H3K79 (H3K79me) affects telomeric heterochromatin structure because mutations at H3K79 as well as inactivation of its methyltransferase, Dot1, lead to loss of telomere silencing (Jones et al., 2008; Ng et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Symmetrical modification of histone lysines within a nucleosome is not globally required in HeLa cells.
source: For example, symmetrical modification of histone lysines within a nucleosome is not globally required in HeLa cells (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: A significant number of nucleosomes contain asymmetrically modified sister histones in different cell types.
source: In addition, in different cell types, a significant number of nucleosomes contain asymmetrically modified sister histones (Fisher and Fisher, 2011; Mikkelsen et al., 2007; Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Asymmetrically modified nucleosomes are present in embryonic stem cells but are symmetrically modified upon differentiation.
source: Furthermore, asymmetrically modified nucleosomes are present in embryonic stem cells but are symmetrically modified upon differentiation (Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Two molecules of histone H3 interact through their carboxy-terminal four-helix bundle to form a homodimer.
source: Previous structural work revealed that two molecules of histone H3 interact through their carboxy-terminal four-helix bundle to form a homodimer (Luger et al., 1997; Ramachandran et al., 2011; White et al., 2001) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to structural studies and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Only the H3A110D and H3L130H pairing was able to support cell viability on a 5-FOA plate.
source: Notably, only the H3A110D and H3L130H pairing was able to support cell viability on a 5-FOA plate (Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), allowing us to infer that the H3A110D and H3L130H mutants form a heterodimer that could be assembled into functional nucleosomes in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutant histones H3A110D and H3L130H equally assembled into nucleosomes.
source: To confirm that mutant histones H3A110D and H3L130H equally assembled into nucleosomes, we epitope-tagged one copy of H3 in H3D/H3H cells with Myc.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The amounts of the co-immunoprecipitated complementary H3A110D and H3L130H histones were identical.
source: We normalized immunoprecipitated myc-H3L130H and myc-H3A110D to the same level. The amounts of the co-immunoprecipitated complementary H3A110D and H3L130H histones were identical (Figure 2A), reflecting an equal incorporation of H3A110D and H3L130H into mononucleosomes in H3D/H3H cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A ChIP assay showed almost the same enrichment of H3A110D and H3L130H at the GAL1 gene promoter.
source: A chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay showed almost the same enrichment of H3A110D and H3L130H at the GAL1 gene promoter (Figure 2B), supporting our conclusion that mutant histones H3A110D and H3L130H were assembled into nucleosomes at a ratio of 1:1 in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The nucleosome array on the GAL10 side of the UAS region displayed a similar digestion pattern in H3D/H3H and WT cells.
source: MNase digestion of the GAL1-10 promoter revealed that the nucleosome array on the GAL10 side of the UAS region displayed a similar digestion pattern in H3D/H3H and WT cells, but the nucleosome array on the GAL1 side showed a more evenly digested pattern in WT cells than in H3D/H3H cells (Figure 2C), suggesting altered nucleosome stability in the GAL1 region in H3D/H3H cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: H3D/H3H mutant and WT cells exhibited identical growth rates in YPD medium at 23°C, 30°C and 37°C.
source: H3D/H3H mutant and WT cells exhibited identical growth rates in yeast extract peptone dextrose (YPD) medium at 23°C, 30°C and 37°C.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: When H3D/H3H cells were challenged by DNA-damage reagents, such as phleomycin or MMS, they showed nearly the same sensitivity as WT cells.
source: In addition, when H3D/H3H cells were challenged by rapamycin (data not shown) or DNA-damage reagents, such as phleomycin or methyl methanesulfonate (MMS), they showed nearly the same sensitivity as WT cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Compared with WT cells, H3D/H3H cells showed a reduced growth rate when cultured in raffinose or glycerol medium.
source: Interestingly, compared with WT cells, H3D/H3H cells showed a reduced growth rate when cultured in raffinose or glycerol medium (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No significant differences in the levels of multiple histone PTMs were found between WT and H3D/H3H strains by western blot.
source: We then checked the levels of multiple histone PTMs in WT and H3D/H3H strains by western blot and found no significant differences (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The global gene expression profile of the H3D/H3H strain was found to be very similar to that of the WT strain.
source: The global gene expression profile of the H3D/H3H strain was found to be very similar to that of the WT strain (Figure 2G), but we did see some genes with expression levels that varied between the H3D/H3Hand WT strains.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Both histone H3 N-terminal and H3K4me3 signals in H3DΔ4–15/H3H and H3D/H3HΔ4–15 cells were reduced to approximately half of those observed in H3D/H3H cells.
source: Both histone H3 N-terminal and H3K4me3 signals in H3DΔ4–15/H3H and H3D/H3HΔ4–15 cells were reduced to approximately half of those observed in H3D/H3H cells (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: H3 N-terminal deletion on one sister H3 did not influence H3K4 methylation on the other.
source: These results indicated that H3 N-terminal deletion on one sister H3 did not influence H3K4 methylation on the other.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing approximately 50% reduction in H3K4me3 in asymmetric deletion mutants.

claim: H3K4me3 in H3DK4R/H3H or H3D/H3HK4R cells was approximately 50% lower than that in H3D/H3H cells.
source: Western blotting showed that H3K4me3 in H3DK4R/H3H or H3D/H3HK4R cells was approximately 50% lower than that in H3D/H3H cells, whereas little difference in H3K36me3 was detected among the tested strains (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: For sister H3 histones in a nucleosome, a lack of K4me3 in one tail did not influence K4me3 in the other tail.
source: For sister H3 histones in a nucleosome, a lack of K4me3 in one tail did not influence K4me3 in the other tail, consistent with the observation in Figure 3B.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing approximately 50% reduction in H3K4me3 in asymmetric K4R mutants.

claim: H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were independent of each other because the decrease in H3K4me3 did not alter the level of H3K36me3.
source: In addition, H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 were independent of each other because the decrease in H3K4me3 did not alter the level of H3K36me3.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing no change in H3K36me3 when H3K4me3 was reduced.

claim: Compared with H3D/H3H cells, H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R single-tail mutant cells showed a two-fold increase in GAL1 mRNA levels.
source: Compared with H3D/H3H cells, H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R single-tail mutant cells showed a two-fold increase in GAL1 mRNA levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Compared with single-tail mutant cells, H3DK4R/H3HK4R double-tail mutant cells showed a further two-fold increase in GAL1 mRNA levels.
source: Compared with single-tail mutant cells, H3DK4R/H3HK4R double-tail mutant cells showed a further two-fold increase in GAL1 mRNA levels (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: GAL1 mRNA levels were inversely proportional to H3K4me3 levels at the GAL1 promoter.
source: GAL1 mRNA levels were inversely proportional to H3K4me3 levels at the GAL1 promoter (Figure 4F), suggesting a tight correlation between induction levels and H3K4me3 abundance.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: A moderate level of Gal4 recruitment to the GAL1 promoter was observed in the asymmetrical H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R mutant strains compared with that in their symmetrical H3D/H3H and H3DK4R/H3HK4R counterparts.
source: A moderate level of Gal4 recruitment to the GAL1 promoter was observed in the asymmetrical H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R mutant strains compared with that in their symmetrical H3D/H3H and H3DK4R/H3HK4R counterparts (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Each K4me3-modified sister histone H3 contributed independently to GAL1 gene transcription.
source: Therefore, each K4me3-modified sister histone H3 contributed independently to GAL1 gene transcription, which is probably recognized and read by the GAL1 activator Gal4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing intermediate levels of GAL1 transcription and Gal4 recruitment in asymmetric K4R mutants.

claim: Deletion of SET1 eliminates H3K4 mono-, di- and tri-methylation.
source: Deletion of SET1 eliminates H3K4 mono-, di- and tri-methylation; deletion of SPP1 affects only H3K4 tri-methylation; and deletion of SDC1 affects di- and tri-methylation of H3K4 (Pinskaya et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Loss of SPP1, SDC1 and SET1 led to the upregulation of GAL1 transcription.
source: As the data show, loss of SPP1, SDC1 and SET1 led to the upregulation of GAL1 transcription, which is consistent with previous findings (Pinskaya et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H and a citation to a prior study.

claim: An intermediate level of GAL1 expression was seen in spp1∆ H3DK4R/H3H and spp1∆ H3D/H3HK4R cells.
source: Meanwhile, an intermediate level of GAL1 expression was seen in spp1∆ H3DK4R/H3H and spp1∆ H3D/H3HK4R cells, whereas no significant difference was found in either sdc1∆ or set1∆ mutants (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: H3K4me2/3 but not mono-methylation of H3K4 on sister H3s contributed the most to GAL1 regulation.
source: As distinguishing between the effects of H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 is difficult, we concluded that H3K4me2/3 but not mono-methylation of H3K4 on sister H3s contributed the most to GAL1 regulation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing intermediate GAL1 expression in spp1∆ mutants but not in sdc1∆ or set1∆ mutants.

claim: The level of H3K36me3 in H3DK36R/H3H or H3D/H3HK36R cells showed an approximately 50% decrease compared with H3D/H3H cells.
source: When compared with H3D/H3H cells, H3DK36R/H3H or H3D/H3HK36R cells showed an approximately 50% decrease in H3K36me3, whereas little difference in H3K4me3 was detected among the tested strains (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Loss of K36me3 on one tail did not affect K36me3 on the other tail.
source: These data indicated that the H3DK36R/H3H or H3D/H3HK36R mutants contained only mimics of asymmetrically deposited K36me3, and loss of K36me3 on one tail did not affect K36me3 on the other tail.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing approximately 50% reduction in H3K36me3 in asymmetric K36R mutants.

claim: H3K36me3 and H3K4me were independently regulated chromatin modifications.
source: In addition, in agreement with the data shown in Figure 4B, H3K36me3 and H3K4me were independently regulated chromatin modifications.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing no change in H3K4me3 when H3K36me3 was reduced.

claim: The loss of K36 methylation on H3 tails resulted in short transcripts of the FLO8, PCA1 and STE11 genes.
source: Northern blot analysis showed that the loss of K36 methylation on H3 tails resulted in short transcripts of the tested genes, consistent with previous findings (Carrozza et al., 2005; Li et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and citations to prior studies.

claim: Asymmetrical H3DK36R/H3H and H3D/H3HK36R cells exhibited an intermediate level of short transcripts compared with H3D/H3H cells and symmetrically mutated H3K36 cells.
source: Compared with H3D/H3H cells and symmetrically mutated H3K36 cells, asymmetrical H3DK36R/H3H and H3D/H3HK36R cells exhibited an intermediate level of short transcripts (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: H4 acetylation levels in H3DK36R/H3H and H3D/H3HK36R cells were intermediate relative to those in H3D/H3H cells and symmetrically mutated H3K36 cells.
source: H4 acetylation (H4ac) levels in H3DK36R/H3H and H3D/H3HK36R cells were intermediate relative to those in H3D/H3H cells and symmetrically mutated H3K36 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: H4ac levels were inversely correlated with H3K36me3 levels in the 3' ORF of the FLO8, PCA1 and STE11 genes.
source: Moreover, H4ac levels were inversely correlated with H3K36me3 levels in the same region (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: In the absence of Set2, the level of H4ac in the tested genes showed no significant differences in H3D/H3H, H3DK36R/H3H, H3D/H3HK36R and H3DK36R/H3HK36R cells.
source: In the absence of Set2, the level of H4ac in the tested genes showed no significant differences in H3D/H3H, H3DK36R/H3H, H3D/H3HK36R and H3DK36R/H3HK36R cells (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: H3K36me3 on either sister histone played an independent regulatory role in suppressing spurious intragenic transcription.
source: In light of these data, we concluded that H3K36me3 on either sister histone played an independent regulatory role in suppressing spurious intragenic transcription.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing intermediate levels of short transcripts and H4ac in asymmetric K36R mutants.

claim: H3K79me2/3 levels in H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells were approximately 50% lower than those in H3D/H3H cells.
source: Western blot analysis revealed that H3K79me2/3 levels in H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells were approximately 50% lower than those in H3D/H3H cells (Figure 6B and C), suggesting the incorporation of asymmetrical H3K79me into chromatin and that the methylation of K79 occurs independently on each sister H3.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: The methylation of K79 occurs independently on each sister H3.
source: Western blot analysis revealed that H3K79me2/3 levels in H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells were approximately 50% lower than those in H3D/H3H cells (Figure 6B and C), suggesting the incorporation of asymmetrical H3K79me into chromatin and that the methylation of K79 occurs independently on each sister H3.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing approximately 50% reduction in H3K79me2/3 in asymmetric K79R mutants.

claim: The K79R mutations on both sister H3s resulted in decreased silencing of COS12, ERR1 and ERR3 genes.
source: As expected, the K79R mutations on both sister H3s resulted in decreased silencing of those genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells containing asymmetrical H3K79me exhibited the same level of silencing loss as that of H3DK79R/H3HK79R or sir2∆ cells.
source: Surprisingly, H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells containing asymmetrical H3K79me exhibited the same level of silencing loss as that of H3DK79R/H3HK79R or sir2∆ cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: K79me levels at the promoters of COS12, ERR1 and ERR3 in H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells decreased to approximately half of those in H3D/H3H cells.
source: A ChIP experiment confirmed that K79me levels at the promoters of the genes tested in H3DK79R/H3H and H3D/H3HK79R cells decreased to approximately half of those in H3D/H3H cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The H4ac level in the ORF region was upregulated in K79R mutated cells.
source: Accordingly, the H4ac level in the ORF region was upregulated in K79R mutated cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: K79me marks on both sister H3s act cooperatively to maintain gene silencing near telomeres.
source: Collectively, these data reveal that K79me marks on both sister H3s act cooperatively to maintain gene silencing near telomeres.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that asymmetric K79R mutants have the same level of silencing loss as double K79R mutants.

claim: H3K4R or H3K79R mutations on either one or two sister histones reduced cell growth in the presence of genotoxins.
source: H3K4R or H3K79R mutations on either one or two sister histones reduced cell growth in the presence of the tested genotoxins.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The H3DK36R/H3HK36R mutant was hypersensitive to phleomycin and mildly sensitive to MMS.
source: Notably, the H3DK36R/H3HK36R mutant was hypersensitive to phleomycin and mildly sensitive to MMS.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Single-tail H3K36R or H3K79R mutants displayed an intermediate level of sensitivity to the genotoxic agents compared with the wild type and corresponding double-tail mutant.
source: Compared with the wild type (H3D/H3H) and corresponding double-tail mutant, single-tail H3K36R or H3K79R mutants displayed an intermediate level of sensitivity to the genotoxic agents.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Single-tail H3K4R mutants displayed less growth in response to phleomycin treatment than did double-tail H3K4R mutants.
source: The H3K4 mutants showed a similar level of sensitivity to HU and MMS, but single-tail H3K4R mutants displayed less growth in response to phleomycin treatment than did double-tail H3K4R mutants (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: In response to DNA damage, H3K36me and H3K79me marks on sister histones functioned independently.
source: Together, these observations suggest that, in response to DNA damage, H3K36me and H3K79me marks on sister histones functioned independently, whereas H3K4me marks on sister histones functioned cooperatively.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing intermediate sensitivity to genotoxins in asymmetric K36R and K79R mutants.

claim: In response to DNA damage, H3K4me marks on sister histones functioned cooperatively.
source: Together, these observations suggest that, in response to DNA damage, H3K36me and H3K79me marks on sister histones functioned independently, whereas H3K4me marks on sister histones functioned cooperatively.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that single-tail H3K4R mutants displayed less growth in response to phleomycin than double-tail mutants.

claim: Of the 6000 genes in the yeast genome, approximately 2500 were altered by the H3K4 to R mutation in response to glucose starvation.
source: Of the 6000 genes in the yeast genome, approximately 2500 were altered by the H3K4 to R mutation in response to glucose starvation.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data.

claim: Over 1500 genes' fold-change in both asymmetrical K4R mutants fell between those of H3D/H3H cells and double K4R mutants.
source: Over 1500 genes' fold-change (MID, as defined in Materials and methods) in both asymmetrical K4R mutants (H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R) fell between those of H3D/H3H cells and double K4R mutants (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 22 genes' fold-changes in asymmetrical K4R mutant cells were nearly the same as those in symmetrical K4R mutant cells, indicating cooperativity of sister K4me at these loci.
source: Statistical analysis by t-test and a gene skewness score (GSS) model described in the Materials and methods revealed that 22 genes' fold-changes in asymmetrical K4R mutant (H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R) cells were nearly the same as those in symmetrical K4R mutant (H3DK4R/H3HK4R) cells (Figure 8A,B; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, Cluster I), indicating cooperativity of sister K4me at these loci.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 8A, B and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The fold-changes of 191 genes in asymmetrical K4R mutant cells exhibited an intermediate state between those in symmetrical K4R mutant and WT cells, suggesting that K4me on sister H3s independently regulates the expression of these genes.
source: The fold-changes of 191 genes in asymmetrical K4R mutant (H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R) cells exhibited an intermediate state between those in symmetrical K4R mutant (H3DK4R/H3HK4R) and WT(H3D/H3H) cells (p<0.05) (Figure 8A,B; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, Cluster II), suggesting that K4me on sister H3s independently regulates the expression of these genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 8A, B and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The fold-changes of 158 genes in asymmetrical K4R mutant cells were nearly the same as those in WT H3D/H3H cells, indicating redundancy of sister K4me at these loci.
source: The fold-changes of 158 genes in asymmetrical K4R mutant (H3DK4R/H3H and H3D/H3HK4R) cells were nearly the same as those in WT H3D/H3H cells (Figure 8A,B; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, Cluster III), indicating redundancy of sister K4me at these loci.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 8A, B and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: An approximately 50% decrease in H3K4me3 in asymmetrical K4R mutants was confirmed in the 5' ORFs of the YOR008C, YMR315W and YLR359W genes.
source: An approximately 50% decrease in H3K4me3 in asymmetrical K4R mutants was confirmed in the 5' ORFs of the YOR008C, YMR315W and YLR359W genes, which belong to the three clusters (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: In response to glucose starvation stress, H3K4me on two sister histones in different gene loci impose their effects on transcription in a cooperative, independent or redundant manner.
source: These assessments suggest that, in response to glucose starvation stress, H3K4me on two sister histones in different gene loci impose their effects on transcription in a cooperative (e.g., Cluster I), independent (e.g., Cluster II) or redundant (e.g., Cluster III) manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the RNA-Seq data showing different patterns of gene expression in the three clusters.

claim: The genes in Cluster I and II were mostly upregulated (log2fold change >0), while the genes in Cluster III were mostly downregulated (log2fold change <0).
source: Interestingly, the genes in Cluster I and II were mostly upregulated (log2fold change >0), while the genes in Cluster III were mostly downregulated (log2fold change <0) (Figure 8B), suggesting that under glucose starvation stress, the transcription of upregulated genes may require more subtle regulation mechanisms, such as asymmetrical modification of sister histones.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Under glucose starvation stress, the transcription of upregulated genes may require more subtle regulation mechanisms, such as asymmetrical modification of sister histones.
source: Interestingly, the genes in Cluster I and II were mostly upregulated (log2fold change >0), while the genes in Cluster III were mostly downregulated (log2fold change <0) (Figure 8B), suggesting that under glucose starvation stress, the transcription of upregulated genes may require more subtle regulation mechanisms, such as asymmetrical modification of sister histones.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the observation that upregulated genes show different patterns of regulation by asymmetric K4me.

claim: Many of the genes in Clusters I, II and III overlapped with genes that are regulated by SET1 deletion.
source: Many of the genes in Clusters I, II and III overlapped with genes that are regulated by SET1 deletion (Figure 8C, I∩set1∆, II∩set1∆ and III∩set1∆, respectively), indicating that these overlapping genes are most probably regulated by K4me rather than the K4R mutation on sister H3s.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: 54 of the genes in the II∩set1∆ group were enriched in the pathways involved in glycometabolism, such as carbon metabolism, TCA cycle, and fructose and mannose metabolism.
source: Remarkably, 54 of the genes in the II∩set1∆ group, which is regulated by sister H3K4me, were enriched in the pathways involved in glycometabolism, such as carbon metabolism, TCA cycle, and fructose and mannose metabolism (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Under glucose starvation stress, a significant proportion of H3K4me-responsive genes are regulated by the fluctuation of H3K4me levels on sister H3s.
source: Therefore, under glucose starvation stress, a significant proportion of H3K4me-responsive genes are regulated by the fluctuation of H3K4me levels on sister H3s.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the KEGG pathway analysis showing enrichment of glycometabolism genes in the II∩set1∆ group.

claim: The independent regulatory mode of sister H3K4me is an important player in response to glucose starvation stress.
source: Further analysis of the fold-changes of the genes in the glycometabolism-associated pathways revealed a pattern similar to that of Cluster II (Figure 8—figure supplement 1G), suggesting that the independent regulatory mode of sister H3K4me is an important player in response to glucose starvation stress.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the analysis of fold-changes in glycometabolism genes shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The on-off regulatory mode for H3K4me is more likely to be applicable to the transcription of genes that do not specifically respond to external stimuli.
source: Collectively, these results support the notions that the on-off regulatory mode for H3K4me is more likely to be applicable to the transcription of genes that do not specifically respond to external stimuli (e.g., genes in the I∩set1∆ and III∩set1∆ groups), whereas the fine-tuning mode evolved to regulate the transcription of genes involved in stress-responsive pathways (e.g., genes in the II∩set1∆ group).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the observation that genes in different clusters show different regulatory patterns.
